statement.p: If z = \left(2x+y\right)e^{x},\qquad x = \ln\mathopen{}\left(u\right),\qquad y = v, find \partial z/\partial u and \partial z/\partial v. The variables are restricted to domains on which the functions are defined.

static.solution: z is a function of two variables x and y which are functions of two variables the two chain rule identities which apply are: \frac{\partial z}{\partial u} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}+ \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u} so \frac{\partial z}{\partial u} = (2e^{x}+\left(2x+y\right)e^{x}) \left(\frac{1}{u}\right) + (e^{x})\cdot 0 = \left(2e^{\ln\mathopen{}\left(u\right)}+\left(2\ln\mathopen{}\left(u\right)+v\right)e^{\ln\mathopen{}\left(u\right)}\right)\frac{1}{u}. and \frac{\partial z}{\partial v} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}+ \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v} so \frac{\partial z}{\partial v} = (2e^{x}+\left(2x+y\right)e^{x})(0) + (e^{x})\cdot (1) = e^{\ln\mathopen{}\left(u\right)}\cdot 1.
